# More everyday tasks: backups, network drives, web checks, world time, Windows features, developer tools, accounts.

## Backups and copies

? backup {src} with today's date | dated backup of {src} | zip {src} with the date | make a backup of {src}
$src = Get-Item -LiteralPath "{{src}}"; $zip = Join-Path "{{dest}}" ('{0} {1:yyyy-MM-dd HHmm}.zip' -f $src.Name, (Get-Date)); Compress-Archive -Path "$($src.FullName)\*" -DestinationPath $zip; Get-Item $zip | Select-Object FullName, @{n='SizeMB';e={[math]::Round($_.Length/1MB,1)}}
= Zips {src} into a file named with today's date and time, saved in {dest}.
& src=. ; dest=$HOME\Documents

? mirror {src} to {dest} | sync {src} to {dest} | keep {dest} in sync with {src}
robocopy "{{src}}" "{{dest}}" /MIR /R:1 /W:1 /NFL /NDL /NP; if ($LASTEXITCODE -lt 8) { $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0; 'Done: {{dest}} now matches {{src}}.' }
= Makes {dest} an exact copy of {src}: files that are not in {src} are DELETED from {dest}.

? copy only new files from {src} to {dest} | incremental backup of {src} to {dest} | copy changed files from {src} to {dest}
robocopy "{{src}}" "{{dest}}" /E /XO /R:1 /W:1 /NFL /NDL /NP; if ($LASTEXITCODE -lt 8) { $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0; 'Copied new and changed files.' }
= Copies files from {src} that are new or newer than the copy in {dest}; nothing is deleted.

? merge all {ext} files in {folder} into one | combine the {ext} files into one file | join text files
Get-ChildItem -Path "{{folder}}\*" -File -Include {{ext}} | Sort-Object Name | Get-Content | Set-Content -Path "{{folder}}\merged.{{ext|raw}}"; Get-Item "{{folder}}\merged.{{ext|raw}}" | Select-Object FullName, Length
= Joins every {ext} file in {folder} (in name order) into merged.{ext}.
& folder=. ; ext=*.txt

? what is in the recycle bin | recycle bin contents | deleted files | items in the recycle bin
$b = (New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application).Namespace(10); $b.Items() | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $_.Name; OriginalFolder = $b.GetDetailsOf($_, 1); Deleted = $b.GetDetailsOf($_, 2); Size = $b.GetDetailsOf($_, 3) } }
= Lists what is in the Recycle Bin, where it came from and when it was deleted.

? restore {file} from the recycle bin | undelete {file} | bring back {file}
$b = (New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application).Namespace(10); $i = $b.Items() | Where-Object Name -like '{{file}}*' | Select-Object -First 1; if ($i) { $i.InvokeVerb('undelete'); "Restored $($i.Name)." } else { 'Not found in the Recycle Bin.' }
= Puts {file} back where it was deleted from.

? symbolic link from {src} to {dest} | create a symlink | link a folder
New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path "{{src}}" -Target "{{dest}}"
= Creates a link at {src} that points to {dest} (needs Developer Mode or admin).

## Network drives and sharing

? mapped network drives | list network drives | which drives are mapped
Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Where-Object DisplayRoot | Select-Object Name, DisplayRoot, @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Free/1GB,1)}}
= Lists drive letters connected to network shares.

? map a network drive {drive} to {path} | connect {path} as drive {drive}
New-PSDrive -Name {{drive}} -PSProvider FileSystem -Root "{{folder}}" -Persist -Scope Global | Select-Object Name, DisplayRoot
= Connects the network share as drive {drive}: (it stays after a restart).
& drive=Z

? disconnect network drive {drive} | remove mapped drive {drive}
Remove-PSDrive -Name {{drive}} -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; net use "{{drive}}:" /delete /y 2>$null; 'Disconnected.'
= Disconnects the network drive {drive}:.

? share {folder} on the network | share this folder
New-SmbShare -Name (Split-Path (Resolve-Path "{{folder}}").Path -Leaf) -Path (Resolve-Path "{{folder}}").Path -ReadAccess Everyone | Select-Object Name, Path
= Shares {folder} on the network (read-only for everyone).
! admin
& folder=.

? stop sharing {name} | remove the share {name}
Remove-SmbShare -Name "{{name}}" -Force; 'Share removed.'
= Stops sharing {name} (the folder itself stays).
! admin

? computers on my network by name | network computers | nas on my network
Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object State -in 'Reachable', 'Stale' | ForEach-Object { $n = try { [Net.Dns]::GetHostEntry($_.IPAddress).HostName } catch { '' }; [pscustomobject]@{ IP = $_.IPAddress; Name = $n } } | Where-Object Name
= Lists devices on your network that have a name.

## Web checks

? website certificate of {host} | when does the ssl certificate of {host} expire | check https of {host}
$c = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new('{{host}}', 443); $s = [Net.Security.SslStream]::new($c.GetStream()); $s.AuthenticateAsClient('{{host}}'); $cert = [Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates.X509Certificate2]$s.RemoteCertificate; $c.Dispose(); [pscustomobject]@{ Site = '{{host}}'; Issuer = $cert.Issuer; Expires = $cert.NotAfter; DaysLeft = ($cert.NotAfter - (Get-Date)).Days }
= Shows who issued the HTTPS certificate of {host} and when it expires.

? title of the website {host} | what is on {host} | page title of {url}
$u = if ('{{url}}' -ne '') { '{{url}}' } else { 'https://{{host}}' }; $r = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $u -TimeoutSec 15; [pscustomobject]@{ Status = $r.StatusCode; Title = ([regex]::Match($r.Content, '<title[^>]*>([^<]*)')).Groups[1].Value.Trim(); SizeKB = [math]::Round($r.RawContentLength/1KB) }
= Downloads the page and shows its status code and title.
& url= ; host=example.com

? response time of {host} | how fast does {host} load
$t = Measure-Command { Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://{{host}}" -TimeoutSec 30 | Out-Null }; '{0} loaded in {1:N0} ms' -f '{{host}}', $t.TotalMilliseconds
= Measures how long https://{host} takes to load.

? weather | weather forecast | what is the weather | weather in {text}
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://wttr.in/$([uri]::EscapeDataString('{{text}}'))?format=3"
= Current weather from wttr.in (needs internet).
& text=

## World time

? what time is it in {tz} | time in {tz} | current time in {tz}
'{0:HH:mm} on {0:dddd} in {1}' -f [TimeZoneInfo]::ConvertTimeBySystemTimeZoneId((Get-Date), '{{tz}}'), '{{tz}}'
= The current time in the {tz} time zone.

? convert {time} to {tz} time | what is {time} here in {tz}
'{0:HH:mm} in {1}' -f [TimeZoneInfo]::ConvertTimeBySystemTimeZoneId((Get-Date '{{time}}'), '{{tz}}'), '{{tz}}'
= Converts {time} (your time) to the {tz} time zone.

## Windows features

? windows features | optional features | which windows features are on
Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online | Where-Object State -eq 'Enabled' | Select-Object FeatureName | Sort-Object FeatureName
= Lists the optional Windows features that are turned on.
! admin

? enable windows sandbox | turn on sandbox
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Containers-DisposableClientVM -All -NoRestart
= Turns on Windows Sandbox (Pro editions; restart afterwards).
! admin

? install wsl | enable linux | install ubuntu
wsl --install
= Installs the Windows Subsystem for Linux with Ubuntu (restart when asked).
! admin

? is a restart pending | is windows waiting for a restart | pending reboot
$keys = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Component Based Servicing\RebootPending', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\WindowsUpdate\Auto Update\RebootRequired'; if ($keys | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ }) { 'Yes - Windows is waiting for a restart.' } else { 'No restart is pending.' }
= Tells you whether Windows is waiting for a restart (after updates).

? is virtualization enabled | vt-x | svm enabled | hyper-v requirements
Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor | Select-Object Name, VirtualizationFirmwareEnabled, VMMonitorModeExtensions
= Shows whether CPU virtualization is turned on in the BIOS.

? uefi or legacy bios | boot mode | is my pc uefi
if (Test-Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecureBoot\State') { 'UEFI' } else { 'Legacy BIOS' }
= Shows whether Windows booted in UEFI or legacy BIOS mode.

? last windows update | when did windows last update
Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending | Select-Object -First 1 HotFixID, Description, InstalledOn
= Shows the most recent Windows update.

? installed fonts | list fonts | which fonts do I have
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Fonts', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Fonts' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.PSObject.Properties | Where-Object Name -notlike 'PS*' | ForEach-Object Name } | Sort-Object -Unique
= Lists the installed fonts.

? install the font {file} | add font {file}
$f = Get-Item -LiteralPath "{{folder}}\{{file}}"; $dir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts"; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir -Force | Out-Null; Copy-Item -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Destination $dir -Force; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Fonts' -Name "$($f.BaseName) (TrueType)" -Value (Join-Path $dir $f.Name); "Installed $($f.Name) for your user (restart open apps to see it)."
% file=ttf,otf,ttc
= Installs the font {file} for your user (no admin rights, no dialogs).
& folder=.

? keyboard layouts | switch keyboard layout | add keyboard language
Start-Process "ms-settings:keyboard"
= Opens keyboard settings (add or remove layouts there; switch with Win+Space).

? default browser | which browser is the default
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell\Associations\UrlAssociations\https\UserChoice' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProgId
= Shows which browser opens web links.

? default apps | change default browser | change default app
Start-Process "ms-settings:defaultapps"
= Opens Default apps settings.

## Accounts

? change my password | change the password of {name}
Start-Process "ms-settings:signinoptions"
= Opens Sign-in options, where you change your password or PIN.

? disable the account {name} | turn off the user {name}
Disable-LocalUser -Name "{{name}}"; Get-LocalUser -Name "{{name}}" | Select-Object Name, Enabled
= Disables the local account {name} (it can't sign in until enabled again).
! admin

? enable the account {name} | turn on the user {name}
Enable-LocalUser -Name "{{name}}"; Get-LocalUser -Name "{{name}}" | Select-Object Name, Enabled
= Enables the local account {name} again.
! admin

? groups of {name} | which groups am I in | my user groups
whoami /groups /fo csv | ConvertFrom-Csv | Where-Object Type -eq 'Alias' | Select-Object 'Group Name'
= Lists the local groups your account belongs to.

## Developer tools

? open vs code here | open this folder in vs code | code .
code .
= Opens the current folder in Visual Studio Code.

? start a web server here | serve this folder over http | local web server
Start-Process python -ArgumentList '-m', 'http.server', '8000' -WorkingDirectory (Get-Location).Path -WindowStyle Minimized; Start-Process 'http://localhost:8000'
= Serves the current folder at http://localhost:8000 (close the minimized window to stop it).

? create a python virtual environment | make a venv | new venv
python -m venv .venv; '.venv created. Activate it with: .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1'
= Creates a Python virtual environment in .venv.

? pip install {text} | install the python package {text}
python -m pip install '{{text}}'
= Installs the Python package {text}.

? python packages | pip list | installed python packages
python -m pip list
= Lists installed Python packages.

? git status | what changed in this repo
git status --short --branch
= Shows the branch and changed files of the Git repository here.

? git pull | update this repo
git pull
= Gets the newest commits from the remote.

? clone {url} | git clone {url}
git clone '{{url}}'
= Downloads the repository into a new folder here.

? new powershell script {file} | create a script {file}
New-Item -ItemType File -Path "{{folder}}\{{file}}" -Force | Out-Null; Set-Content -Path "{{folder}}\{{file}}" -Value "# {{file}}`n`n"; notepad "{{folder}}\{{file}}"
= Creates {file} and opens it in Notepad.
& folder=.

? run the script {file} | execute {file}
& "{{folder}}\{{file}}"
= Runs {file} in Sensei's session.
& folder=.

? json from {url} | call the api {url} | get json from {url}
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri '{{url}}' | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6
= Calls {url} and prints the JSON answer.

## Alex's apps

? open kaizen | start kaizen | kaizen 5s | tidy my pc with kaizen
$l = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Kaizen 5S\Kaizen.exe", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Kaizen 5S.lnk", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Kaizen.lnk") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l } else { 'Kaizen is not installed.' }
= Opens Kaizen 5S, the PC tidying app.

? open morph | start morph | convert a file with morph
$l = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Morph\Morph.exe", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Morph.lnk") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l } else { 'Morph is not installed.' }
= Opens Morph, the file converter.

? open washi | start washi | edit a pdf | pdf editor
$l = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Washi\Washi.exe", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Washi.lnk") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l } else { 'Washi is not installed.' }
= Opens Washi, the PDF editor.

? open tansu | start tansu | archive files with tansu
$l = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Tansu\Tansu.exe", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Tansu.lnk") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l } else { 'Tansu is not installed.' }
= Opens Tansu, the archiver.

? open muda | start muda | which processes waste resources
$l = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Muda\Muda.exe", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Muda.lnk") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l } else { 'Muda is not installed.' }
= Opens Muda, the process waste analyser.

? open tatami | start tatami | disk space map | what is filling my disk visually
$l = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Tatami\Tatami.exe", "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop'))\Tatami.lnk") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l } else { 'Tatami is not installed.' }
= Opens Tatami, the disk space map.

## Any app by name

? open {pkg} | start {pkg} | launch {pkg} | run the app {pkg}
$q = '{{pkg}}'; $a = Get-StartApps | Where-Object Name -like "*$q*" | Sort-Object { $_.Name.Length } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($a) { Start-Process "shell:AppsFolder\$($a.AppID)"; "Opening $($a.Name)" } else { $l = Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu", "$env:ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu", ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop')) -Recurse -Filter "*$q*.lnk" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1; if ($l) { Invoke-Item $l.FullName; "Opening $($l.BaseName)" } else { "No app called $q found in the Start menu." } }
= Finds "{pkg}" in the Start menu and opens it.

? close {pkg} | quit {pkg}
$p = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowHandle -ne 0 -and ($_.ProcessName -like '*{{pkg}}*' -or $_.MainWindowTitle -like '*{{pkg}}*') }; if ($p) { $p | ForEach-Object { [void]$_.CloseMainWindow(); "Asked $($_.ProcessName) to close." } } else { 'No open window matches "{{pkg}}".' }
= Asks the program whose name or window title matches "{pkg}" to close normally.
